import html # Template for the invitation (must not be altered by user input) INVITATION_FORMAT = """

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
Additional notes: {additional_notes}
""" def render_event_invitation( event_title: str, event_description: str, event_date: str, additional_notes: str ) -> str: """ Render a sanitized HTML invitation from user-provided data. Parameters ---------- event_title : str Title of the event. event_description : str Full description (may contain line breaks). event_date : str Date of the event. additional_notes : str Any extra notes from the user. Returns ------- str Sanitized HTML content ready for safe rendering on a web page. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the required arguments is not a string. """ # Validate types to avoid accidental injection via non-string objects for name, value in [ ("event_title", event_title), ("event_description", event_description), ("event_date", event_date), ("additional_notes", additional_notes), ]: if not isinstance(value, str): raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a string") # Escape user input to neutralize any HTML/JS injection attempts safe_title = html.escape(event_title, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(event_description, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") safe_date = html.escape(event_date, quote=True) safe_notes = html.escape(additional_notes, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") # Construct the final HTML rendered = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes ) return rendered.strip()
